extracted.intended_audience: researchers seeking Cancer Research UK funding and research support (primarily UK-based cancer researchers)
extracted.subtask_short: applying for Cancer Research UK funding
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Cancer Research UK's research strategy, funding priorities, types of support, networks and career-development offerings for researchers. The page describes the topics, project types and cultural/organizational expectations that CRUK funds and supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding strategic priorities (four primary objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund research across four primary objectives – discovery, detection, prevention and treatment – to build a deeper understanding of every aspect of cancer that will ultimately lead to longer, healthier lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is CRUK's high-level view of what kinds of research they prioritise; proposals should align to one or more of these objectives to be of interest. The page frames funding decisions around these strategic objectives rather than a single disease or method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery research priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery: Research in fundamental biology, genetics and immunology, biomarker discovery and preclinical studies, imaging and radiotherapy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK supports fundamental and preclinical work that advances basic understanding of cancer biology and enables downstream applications (e.g., biomarkers, imaging). Proposals in these topic areas are within CRUK's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early detection and diagnosis priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Early detection and diagnosis: Research in early detection of cancers and pre-cancerous changes, underlying biology of cancers, cancer emergence and progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that improves detection, diagnosis, or understanding of early-stage cancer or precursor lesions is explicitly prioritised. Emphasis on biology underpinning detection and progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention and population priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevention and population: Research into cancer epidemiology, risk, incidence, survival and preventative interventions including fundamental biological insights related to cancer prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK funds population-level and preventive research, including epidemiology, risk/survival studies and interventions aimed at preventing cancer, as well as foundational biology relevant to prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical: Research across the clinical pathway, including high-impact early phase and first-in-human trials and ambitious and innovative trial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical proposals should demonstrate potential for high impact across the clinical pathway; CRUK particularly highlights early phase, first-in-human studies and innovative trial designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for work that spans strategic priorities (translational/cross-cutting support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other opportunities: We also support research and translation that spans our strategic priorities. Access the support you need to maximise the impact of your work in these areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK offers additional schemes/targeted support for projects that cut across the four main objectives or focus on enabling areas (see listed thematic supports such as research data, cancers of unmet need, children's cancers, and translation/drug development). Applicants should explore these tailored opportunities if their work is cross-cutting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data support
rubrics_metrics.description: Research data: Discover support to maximise the impact of your research data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK provides resources or support related to research data management and reuse to maximise research impact. Applicants should consider data strategy and available CRUK data-support services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: cancers of unmet need
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancers of unmet need: Explore our work in brain, lung, oesophagus, pancreas, liver and stomach cancers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK explicitly highlights certain tumour types as areas of unmet need; proposals addressing these cancers may align with strategic priorities and dedicated initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: children's and young people's cancers
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's and young people's cancers: Get involved in children’s and young people’s cancer research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is targeted support and emphasis on paediatric and adolescent/young-adult cancer research. Applicants in these areas should consult relevant CRUK programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research translation and drug development
rubrics_metrics.description: Research translation and drug development: Translate your research into real-world impact. Our translational arm, Cancer Research Horizons, offers support wherever you are in the translational pathway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK places value on work that moves discoveries toward clinical or commercial impact; Cancer Research Horizons provides translational support. Proposals with clear translational plans or drug-development pathways are encouraged to engage with these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of funding mechanisms supported
rubrics_metrics.description: We fund individual projects, fellowships, large-scale team programmes, multidisciplinary collaborations and international consortia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK offers a range of grant/funding mechanisms from individual awards to large collaborative and international programmes. Applicants should select mechanisms that match the scale and scope of their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research network and infrastructure support
rubrics_metrics.description: Our world-class research network: Our research institutes, translational research centres, national network and partnerships provide a UK-wide ecosystem with capabilities across the research and translational pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK emphasises institutional and network capacity (core-funded institutes, translational centres and partnerships). Proposals that leverage or contribute to this network, or that demonstrate institutional capability, may be favoured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research careers and development support
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop your research career: We develop outstanding cancer researchers through funding, mentoring and coaching, training and networking opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK provides career-development support (mentoring, coaching, training). Fellowship and early-career applicants should consider these offerings and demonstrate how the award will support career progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of a positive research culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Thrive in a positive research culture: We use our voice as a research funder to bring about change, shape and influence research environments to be inclusive, open and supportive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK expects funded research environments to be inclusive, open and supportive; applicants should consider and describe how their teams and environments meet these cultural expectations (e.g., inclusion, research integrity, open practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and dissemination via events
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific events and webinars: We host scientific and translational conferences, workshops, webinars and other events. Join us to hear about the latest science, present your own research and network with our exceptional community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRUK provides platforms for dissemination, networking and professional development. Applicants and awardees are encouraged to engage with these events to present findings and build collaborations.
